reconciliation.note: SitRep65 prints a FULL cumulative per-zone table (Tableau 2), transcribed here and visually verified against the page-3 render. Named health-zone rows excluding the 17-case Ituri unventilated residual sum to 2327 confirmed; with that residual they reconcile to the 2344 DRC total. Table 1 province totals: Ituri 2090/776, Nord-Kivu 230/139, Sud-Kivu 3/1, Haut-Uele 16/10, Tshopo 5/4 = national 2344/930, and every province's zone rows sum EXACTLY to its Table 1 total (Nord-Kivu closes cleanly this cycle with Katwa 98/71 and no over-count, unlike SitRep63/64). The national cumulative is additive-with-harmonization from SitRep64: 2267 + 83 gross new confirmations (Ituri 67, Nord-Kivu 16) - 6 harmonization removal = 2344, and 893 + 40 - 3 = 930. The harmonization (cover asterisk) revised Haut-Uele 22/13 -> 16/10 by removing 6 previously double-counted confirmed cases and 3 deaths reconciled against Ituri's Nia-Nia zone; Ituri rose exactly +67 (its day notifications) and Nia-Nia only +2, so the 6 cases were a net de-duplication, NOT a province-to-province transfer. The +83/+40 gross day figures must not be read as the national increment. The single DRC unallocated residual is the 17-case Ituri unventilated block (country-scope 37 with the 20 Uganda anchor). Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) prints 52 days with no new confirmed case (unchanged from SitRep64's 52; the counter did not advance and is carried as printed), so 46 zones are touched and 45 are actively transmitting.

lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 167 samples documented in the collection network / 67 positive (45 living, 22 deaths) = 38.1%; Nord-Kivu 127 analyzed / 16 positive = 12.6%. Positivity uses 83 positives over 294 analyzed samples (Ituri + Nord-Kivu). Haut-Uele (53 collected) and Tshopo (6 collected) samples are in analysis and carry no positivity, so they are excluded from the 24h analyzed denominator. The day's laboratory positives (67 + 16 = 83) EQUAL the gross day confirmations exactly this cycle, unlike SitRep64's off-by-one at Nord-Kivu. Ituri's apparent positivity rose to 38.1% (167 -> a smaller documented denominator than SitRep64's 211) which is a test-targeting movement, not a measured prevalence change.

care_continuity: SitRep65 Tableau 6: 724 in isolation at end of day (272 confirmed / 452 suspected, a split that CLOSES exactly against the census this cycle) at 84.5% global bed occupancy (724/857 beds); Ituri 76.3% (539/706), Nord-Kivu 123.1% (181/141), Tshopo 40.0% (4/10); Haut-Uele reports ND. The bed identity closes exactly at every level (707 J-1 + 121 admissions - 104 exits = 724; Ituri 540 + 71 - 72 = 539; Nord-Kivu 166 + 47 - 32 = 181; Tshopo 1 + 3 - 0 = 4). Exits over 24h (104 total): 14 deaths, 63 non-cases, 22 recoveries, 4 escapes, 1 HGR transfer. Ituri first-line personnel: 119 cumulative infections, 61 recovered, 22 hospitalized, 36 deaths (CFR 30.3%).

The implied prior baseline of 444 confirms that SitRep64's promoted 412 was understated (its own component reconstruction gave 443-444) and has now been reconciled by the source, so the apparent 412 -> 466 jump is a correction artifact and the true daily gain is +22. highlights: 83 gross new confirmed cases (Ituri 67, Nord-Kivu 16) and 40 gross new deaths (Ituri 31, Nord-Kivu 9); after a data harmonization that removed 6 double-counted confirmed cases and 3 deaths from Haut-Uele, the DRC cumulative moves +77/+37 to 2344 confirmed / 930 deaths (CFR 39.7%). Haut-Uele is revised 22/13 -> 16/10; no other province lost cases, so the harmonization is a net de-duplication reconciled against Ituri's Nia-Nia zone rather than a transfer. The +83/+40 gross figures must not be read as national incidence.

Contact follow-up held at 85.8% nationally (10517/12251), still below the 95% threshold but on a denominator that GREW by 431 (11820 -> 12251) with the province rows summing exactly to the national totals, a healthier signal than SitRep64's -1751 denominator drop. Ituri 84.9% (7886/9285), Nord-Kivu 88.4% (2553/2888), Tshopo 100.0% (78/78); Haut-Uele ND, Sud-Kivu follow-up closed.

No new health zone was affected: the roster holds at 46 touched and 45 actively transmitting, with Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) printing 52 days without a confirmed case. The day's new cases concentrate at Nizi (30), Bunia (15) and Rwampara (10) in Ituri, with Ituri holding 89.1% of cumulative cases; Nord-Kivu adds at Katwa (6), Musienene (4), Beni (3), Butembo (2) and Kyondo (1). Every province's zone rows sum exactly to its Table 1 total and Nord-Kivu closes with no over-count.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 18/07): 872 alerts of the day (864 new + 8 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo (Sud-Kivu reports none). Investigated 94.6% (825/872): Ituri 86.4% (293/339), Nord-Kivu 100.0% (525/525), Haut-Uele 100.0% (4/4), Tshopo 75.0% (3/4). Every column reconciles exactly: province rows sum to the national totals for alerts (872), investigated (825), validated-living (112 = 72+33+4+3), validated-deceased (80 = 56+24+0+0) and suspects (192 = 128+57+4+3), and the Report-J-1/new split closes (8 + 864 = 872). Validated suspects 192 = 112 living + 80 community deaths under investigation. Ituri's investigation rate eased to 86.4% from 90.9% while Nord-Kivu cleared 100% of a heavy 525-alert load.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge; activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of frontline providers (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; return to work announced after the Ituri military governor's intervention) interrupts response activities including dignified and secure burials.
challenges.response: Regularize provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: 123.1% occupancy in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 76.3% in Ituri (539 patients for 706 beds), carrying admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk. Figures match the SitRep65 Tableau 6 (current, not carried).
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures, and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance remains weak, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted: Ituri 84.9%, Nord-Kivu 88.4%, national 85.8%, below the 95% threshold. Figures match the SitRep65 Tableau 4 (current).
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision, and investigate the drop observed in Ituri.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and weak prepositioning at points of control, causing transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Preposition ambulances including at PoE/PoC, and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs, weakening overall case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%), carrying a high nosocomial-infection risk against 119 cumulative first-line personnel infections including 36 deaths.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) combined with high mobility, carrying urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion risk.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority Haut-Uele PoE/PoC and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories at Butembo, Mambasa and Logo are still being installed, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralized diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of CEHS.

The province rows sum EXACTLY to the national totals (9285+2888+78 = 12251 under follow-up; 7886+2553+78 = 10517 seen), and the cover KPI agrees, so no rate cluster is in conflict. Unlike SitRep64 (denominator -1751), the population under follow-up ROSE from 11820 to 12251 (+431) while coverage held at ~85.8%, a healthier signal: the cohort grew and was still worked at the same rate. The section-3.3 narrative prose inverts Ituri's numerator and denominator ('9285 contacts sur 7886'); the table values (9285 under / 7886 seen) are promoted.

priorities.priority: Lift national contact follow-up above the 95% threshold from 85.8% (Ituri 84.9%, Nord-Kivu 88.4%) and investigate the Ituri drop, while sustaining the alert investigation recovery (national 94.6%, Nord-Kivu 100%).
Relieve Nord-Kivu isolation saturation at 123.1% (181 patients, 141 beds) and re-establish systematic bed-capacity reporting; Haut-Uele carries no Tableau-6 column this cycle.
Complete and document the Haut-Uele / Nia-Nia harmonization that removed 6 confirmed cases and 3 deaths from the cumulative, so the +83/+40 gross day figures are not mistaken for national incidence.

Keep the Uganda-border and Haut-Uele extension axes in view; activate the 23 priority Haut-Uele PoE/PoC and sustain screening across the 75 combined Ituri + Nord-Kivu points that registered 149285 travellers.
Sustain residual epidemiological surveillance in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa prints 52 days with no new confirmed case, toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep65 national headline is DRC-only (2344 confirmed / 930 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 2364 confirmed / 932 deaths / 477 recovered.

DATA HARMONIZATION (cover asterisk): Haut-Uele is revised from SitRep64's 22 confirmed / 13 deaths to 16 / 10 by removing 6 previously double-counted confirmed cases and 3 deaths, reconciled against Ituri's Nia-Nia health zone. Ituri rose exactly +67 (its own day notifications) and Nia-Nia only +2, so the 6 removed cases were a net de-duplication, NOT a province-to-province transfer. Consequently the printed +83 new cases (Ituri 67 + Nord-Kivu 16) and +40 deaths (Ituri 31 + Nord-Kivu 9) are gross daily notifications that foot to a +77 / +37 cumulative movement (2267 + 83 - 6 = 2344; 893 + 40 - 3 = 930). new_confirmed_24h is carried at the printed 83 and must not be differenced against the cumulative without the harmonization term.

Haut-Uele CFR disagrees within the document: Table 1 prints 62.5% and Table 2's province row prints 62.2%; the arithmetic 10/16 = 62.5% is promoted and the 62.2% preserved as a typo. The Haut-Uele zone split changed under the harmonization (Wamba 16/8 -> 6/3, Boma Mangbetu 2/1 -> 4/2, Isiro 1/1 -> 3/2, Pawa 3/3 unchanged) and the province is footnoted as reclassified, so no trend is fitted to it.

Nord-Kivu isolation occupancy prints 123.1% against 181 patients / 141 beds, which computes to 128.4%; the printed 123.1% implies a ~147-bed denominator. The 181 census and 141 beds are carried as printed and no derived Nord-Kivu occupancy is published; the printed 123.1% is preserved as an internal inconsistency.
The Ituri Tableau-6 bed count prints 706 while the section-4 prose says '716 lits'. Tableau 6's 706 is promoted (the 76.3% occupancy = 539/706 is consistent with it); the prose 716 is a typo.

Recovered advanced to 466 DRC cumulative (+22: Ituri 21, Nord-Kivu 1), implying a prior-cycle baseline of 444. SitRep64 promoted the cover's stale 412 while its own component reconstruction gave 443-444; SitRep65's 466 = ~444 + 22 confirms that the SitRep64 recovered series was understated by ~32 and has now been reconciled by the source. The cross-cycle recovered movement 412 -> 466 (+54) is therefore an artifact of the SitRep64 understatement; the true daily is +22 on the corrected ~444 baseline. Country-scope recovered 477 (+11 Uganda anchor).

The contact denominator ROSE from 11820 to 12251 (+431) with coverage stable at 85.8%, and the province rows sum exactly to the national totals, so unlike SitRep64 there is no unexplained denominator drop and no competing rate cluster. Tshopo prints 78/78 = 100.0%, a full-coverage point rather than a carried-forward row.

Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) prints 52 consecutive days with no new confirmed case, unchanged from SitRep64's 52 (the counter did not advance a day); it is carried as printed. 46 health zones are affected but only 45 carry active transmission, the two counts carried separately.

The cover per-province CFR line (Ituri 37.1%, Nord-Kivu 60.4%, Haut-Uele 62.5%, Sud-Kivu 33.3%, Tshopo 80.0%) agrees with Table 1 for all five provinces (776/2090 = 37.1%; 139/230 = 60.4%; 10/16 = 62.5%; 1/3 = 33.3%; 4/5 = 80.0%).
